## Executive summary

This report documents the corrected FraudDetect analytical workflow using 10,000 simulated financial transactions. It compares supervised fraud classifiers, evaluates a training-only Isolation Forest with validation-derived alert thresholds, and explores investigation-cost scenarios.

**Scope limitation:** The data are simulated. Performance metrics are not evidence of performance on real financial institution transactions. Financial estimates use transaction amount as an exposure proxy and explicit illustrative assumptions. They are not realized losses, actual recoveries, or validated savings.

## Reproducibility and inputs

Run the corrected pipeline from the repository root before rendering this report:

```r
source("corrected_r/scripts/01_modeling.R")
source("corrected_r/scripts/04_optimize_anomaly_thresholds.R")
source("corrected_r/scripts/05_cost_sensitive_alert_optimization.R")
```

The report reads generated CSVs from `corrected_r/outputs/`. It does not rerun the original historical scripts.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
out_dir <- "corrected_r/outputs"

model_metrics <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "model_comparison.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
policy_metrics <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "if_threshold_policy_comparison.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
cost_comparison <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "cost_sensitive_policy_comparison.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
cost_sensitivity <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "cost_sensitivity_analysis.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
assumptions <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "cost_model_assumptions.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
importance <- read_csv(file.path(out_dir, "rf_variable_importance.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Data partition and evaluation design

The modeling script creates mutually exclusive stratified partitions:

| Partition | Share | Role |
|---|---:|---|
| Training | 60% | Fit supervised models and Isolation Forest |
| Validation | 20% | XGBoost early stopping and threshold selection |
| Test | 20% | Final held-out evaluation |

Classification thresholds are selected on validation data. Isolation Forest is fitted using training features only, without fraud labels. Anomaly-score thresholds are selected from validation-score quantiles and then evaluated on the held-out test set.

## Supervised model comparison

```{r}
model_metrics |>
  select(model, test_roc_auc, test_pr_auc, precision, recall, specificity,
         false_positives, false_negatives) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Held-out test performance")
```

XGBoost achieved the strongest ROC-AUC and PR-AUC among the three evaluated candidates in this run. At its validation-selected operating threshold, the test evaluation recorded 491 alerts, 79 true positives, and 412 false positives. This is a model comparison on synthetic data, not a production performance claim.

### ROC-AUC and PR-AUC

```{r}
model_metrics |>
  select(model, test_roc_auc, test_pr_auc) |>
  pivot_longer(-model, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(metric = recode(metric,
                         test_roc_auc = "ROC-AUC",
                         test_pr_auc = "PR-AUC")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(model, value), y = value, fill = metric)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "AUC", fill = NULL,
       title = "Held-out model discrimination") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Random Forest permutation importance

```{r}
importance |>
  slice_max(permutation_importance, n = 12) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(feature, permutation_importance),
             y = permutation_importance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2874a6") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Permutation importance",
       title = "Random Forest feature importance") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Permutation importance describes how predictive performance changes when a feature is permuted in this fitted model. It does not establish causality.

## Anomaly detection and alert-policy trade-offs

The table below compares validation-threshold policies on the held-out test partition.

```{r}
policy_metrics |>
  filter(split == "test") |>
  select(strategy, target_validation_alert_rate, alerts,
         true_positives, false_positives, false_negatives,
         precision, recall, specificity) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Anomaly and combined alert policies on test data")
```

The OR policy can increase fraud recall by adding anomaly alerts to XGBoost alerts, but it also increases investigation volume and false positives. The AND policy is more restrictive and generally trades recall for precision. A validation target rate does not guarantee the same alert rate on the test set.

## Cost-sensitive investigation scenarios

### Assumptions

```{r}
assumptions |> kable(caption = "Illustrative financial assumptions")
```

Transaction amount is used as a proxy for fraud exposure. Missed-fraud exposure and the unrecovered share of detected-fraud exposure are scenario calculations. They are not observed realized losses or verified recoveries.

### Policy comparison

```{r}
cost_comparison |>
  arrange(estimated_total_cost) |>
  select(strategy, alerts, true_positives, false_positives,
         false_negatives, total_alert_review_cost,
         estimated_missed_fraud_loss, estimated_total_cost) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Estimated costs under default assumptions")
```

### Sensitivity analysis

```{r}
cost_sensitivity |>
  group_by(review_cost_per_alert, recovery_share_when_detected) |>
  slice_min(estimated_total_cost, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(review_cost_per_alert, recovery_share_when_detected,
         strategy, alerts, estimated_total_cost) |>
  arrange(review_cost_per_alert, recovery_share_when_detected) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Lowest estimated-cost policy by scenario")
```

Operational capacity is a separate constraint. The Shiny dashboard applies an editable alert-capacity filter before showing feasible policies. Cost rankings are conditional on the assumed review cost, loss severity, recovery share, and available investigation capacity.

## Limitations

- The dataset is simulated and may not reflect real fraud prevalence, feature distributions, adversarial behavior, or operational workflows.
- A single held-out split provides uncertain estimates. Temporal validation and independent external data would be needed for stronger evidence.
- Synthetic feature relationships do not establish causal fraud drivers.
- Transaction amount is only an exposure proxy. Institution-specific loss, recovery, and investigation-cost data are needed for credible financial estimates.
- The dashboard is an analytical demonstration, not a real-time scoring service or case-management system.
- No production monitoring, model drift controls, or deployment architecture is implemented.

## Interactive dashboard

After generating the corrected outputs, launch the dashboard from the repository root:

```r
shiny::runApp("shiny/")
```

The dashboard provides an executive overview, fraud patterns, supervised model comparison, anomaly-policy comparison, cost-sensitive financial analysis, and a held-out transaction explorer.
